query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser melting deposition, high entropy alloy, deep cryogenic treatment, 3D printing, defects, strength–ductility synergistic improvement

At present, the casting forming of HEAs is facing some problems due to their high melt viscosity, and laser additive manufacturing (AM) technology can effectively solve this problem [,,]. Laser melting deposition (LMD) technology has high energy density and complex-shape-forming ability, which can solve the problem of HEA forming and accumulate thermal stress in as-deposited alloy samples []. At the same time, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) has been gradually applied as a method to uniformly aggravate the residual stress generated by LMD, and remarkable results have been achieved []. In previous studies, the DCT method has often been used to modify FCC structural metals by constructing twins [,]. In this paper, LMD forming and DCT treatment were carried out on the previously designed lower-density Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy in which the atoms of Hf and Ta are 25% of the atoms of other elements, in order to achieve a strength–ductility synergistic improvement by increasing the internal stress and lattice distortion so as to make up for the performance degradation caused by the decrease in density compared with the equiatomic ratio system. In summary, the DCT method effectively increases the participating stress value accumulated in the LMD process, further induces the lattice distortion of the alloy, improves the plasticity of Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy, and promotes crystal line defects to improve the strength of the alloy. LMD–DCT has been proven to be an effective method of synergistically improving the strength and plasticity of the alloy. Furthermore, DCT with a long immersion time can avoid a large degree of processing deformation and directly promote the formation of HCP precipitates near the grain boundary position. The presence of precipitates further improves the strength of the alloy. The DCT method can effectively utilize the residual stress accumulated in the alloy during the forming process of laser additive manufacturing methods such as LMD. Compared with traditional rolling methods, the DCT method is more suitable for the modification of complex shape parts formed by LMD near-net forming. For HfNbTaTiZr alloy, DCT can also be targeted for phase control. It can be said that DCT is an excellent supporting scheme for additive manufacturing. decision.rationale: The intervention of deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) after selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing addresses the problem of improving dimensional precision and mechanical integrity by reducing defects and improving grain structure. The critic's review suggests that the DCT method is effective in increasing the participating stress value, inducing lattice distortion, and improving the strength and plasticity of the alloy. However, further research is needed to explore the effect of DCT on different high-entropy alloys and operating conditions. Therefore, the chosen direction is to adopt the DCT intervention with the critic's fix to explore its effect on various high-entropy alloys and operating conditions.
